rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation delivered about the Cave and related matters is the truth from God, refuting the interlocutors’ claims.
rows.anchor: الوحي العربي العري عن العوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge addresses everyone: faith is accepted even in poverty, while rejection merits disregard and eventual divine vengeance despite worldly wealth or status.
rows.anchor: مقبول مرغوب فيه وإن كان فقيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both faith and unbelief depend on God’s created will: voluntary action requires an intention, and tracing prior intentions infinitely is impossible.
rows.anchor: لأن الفعل الاختياري يمتنع حصوله بدون القصد إليه وذلك القصد إن كان بقصد آخر يتقدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God must create the initiating intention, compelling the act while the human appears to choose; therefore the verse does not support the Muʿtazilites.
rows.anchor: فوجب أن تنتهي تلك القصود إلى قصد يخلقه الله في العبد على سبيل الضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepared fire is for wrongdoers, meaning unbelievers, and its enclosure surrounds them like a fence around a tent.
rows.anchor: حائطها الذي يدار حولها كما يدار الحظير حول الخيمة من جميع الجوانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea for rain or relief is answered mockingly with molten, thick, intensely hot liquid, compared to thin pitch, melted metal, or oil dregs.
rows.anchor: وهو القطران الرقيق وما ذاب في صفر أو حديد والزيت أو درديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The liquid scorches faces when brought near the mouth, so its effect on the mouth and insides is worse.
rows.anchor: أي إذا قرب إلى الفم فكيف بالفم والجوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drink is vile: black, foul-smelling, thick, and hot; the fire is an evil lodging prepared for rest.
rows.anchor: فإنه أسود منتن غليظ حار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith means submitting to commands, and righteous deeds verify that submission.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإيمان هو الإذعان للأوامر ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God never wastes the reward of those who do good, whose deeds earn the description of excellence.
rows.anchor: أي بوجه من الوجوه لما يقتضيه عظمتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eden means abiding, and rivers flow beneath the believers’ dwellings.
rows.anchor: إلى أنهم استحقوا بذلك الوصف بالإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording for adornment focuses on its occurrence; its rarity means it is bestowed from the unseen by God.
rows.anchor: إنما يؤتى بها من الغيب فضلا من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Armlets of gold resemble ornaments worn by worldly kings, including Persian unbelievers.
rows.anchor: كما يلبس ذلك ملوك الدنيا من جبابرة الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their green garments are silk: sundus is fine and istabraq is coarse; they recline in comfort on couches.
rows.anchor: وهو ما رق من الديباج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is an excellent reward and resting place, even beyond the descriptions already given.
rows.anchor: فكيف ولها من الأوصاف ما لا يعلمه حق علمه إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed pronoun in “He is God” conveys that God is at once supremely manifest and beyond concealment; it may refer to the one who created the addressee.
rows.anchor: إلى ذلك جميعا بإضماره قبل الذكر فقال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the speaker’s Lord and benefactor; creatures are His servants, so a servant cannot share the Lord’s place.
rows.anchor: فإن الكل خلقه وعبيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and poverty both come from God; relying on wealth as an independent source of security is associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: فإني لا أرى الغنى والفقر إلا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer teaches the garden owner to remember God’s will on entering, echoing the instruction not to assert certainty about future events.
rows.anchor: لا تفرح بها ولا بغيرها مما يفنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What God wills” covers what He wills in the present and future, whether already manifest or still to come; the response is left unstated for that breadth.
rows.anchor: لا ما يشاؤه غيره ولا يشاؤه هو سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “There is no power except through God” affirms God’s power and the servant’s disavowal of independent power, and teaches that created capacity depends on His determination.
rows.anchor: لا قدرة لأحد من الخلق إلا بتقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase also refutes philosophers who treat natural properties as independently effective.
rows.anchor: على فساد قول الفلاسفة في الطبائع من أنها مؤثرة بنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer acknowledges having less wealth and children, the latter being a person’s dearest dependents, unlike the other man’s boastful pride.
rows.anchor: أي من جهة المال والولد الذي هو أعز نفر الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer expects God to grant him something better than the garden and to send projectiles of lightning and severe hail against it.
rows.anchor: أي مرامي من الصواعق والبرد الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A slippery, bare surface results when its vegetation is eradicated, leaving neither growth nor a foothold.
rows.anchor: أرضا يزلق عليها لملاستها باستئصال نباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the garden’s water “a sinking” uses a verbal noun for emphasis; its owner then cannot retrieve it.
rows.anchor: وصف بالمصدر لأنه أبلغ { فلن تستطيع }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden’s entire produce was destroyed; the passive construction emphasizes the comprehensive ruin without naming a particular agent and suggests its ease.
rows.anchor: بني للمفعول لأن الفكر حاصل بإحاطة الهلاك من غير نظر إلى فاعل مخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner turns his hands in regret, striking one against the other over what he spent cultivating and improving the garden.
rows.anchor: ويضرب إحداهما على الأخرى تحسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden lies empty and collapsed: its supports fell, then the structure they carried fell over them.
rows.anchor: وهي خاوية } أي ساقطة مع الخلو { على عروشها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wish not to have associated anyone with God is regret over worldly loss, not concern for faith or salvation; his understanding remains bound to visible things.
rows.anchor: لقصور عقله ووقوفه مع المحسوسات المشاهدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No faction, whether his own supporters or others, could rescue him apart from God, and he could not defend himself.
rows.anchor: ينصرونه } مما وقع فيه { من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with fatḥ means help or victory; the kasr reading, transmitted from Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, means authority, and the author reconciles them as one verbal noun and sense.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة حمزة والكسائي , والفتح لغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers put “the True” in the genitive as an adjective, while Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read it in the nominative as a new, detached clause.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بالجر على الوصف وهو في قراءة أبي عمرو والكسائي بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God in dire crisis proves He is true and all else false; pride in temporary possessions is foolish, and poverty is no reason to shame or expel believers.
rows.anchor: برهان قاطع على أنه الحق وما سواه باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ poverty may soon become wealth and their weakness strength.
rows.anchor: وأنه يوشك أن يعود فقرهم غنى وضعفهم قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the best reward and outcome; the morphological form of “outcome” conveys abundance or intensity.
rows.anchor: من صيغ جموع الكثرة فيفيده ذلك مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life for everyone resembles rain-fed vegetation: it becomes lush and varied, then withers, breaks apart, and is scattered, exposing the world’s brief allure.
rows.anchor: في ينوعها ونضرتها , واختلابها للنفوس ببهجتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain descends from above by God’s power and at the needed time; the water mingles with soil and produces varied, dense growth that God later dries.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على بليغ القدرة في إمساكه في العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Withered debris” means dry, crumbled vegetation; the winds stir it, scatter it, and carry it away.
rows.anchor: أي تثيره وتفرقه وتذهب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s power to create, destroy, and restore is eternal, not newly acquired.
rows.anchor: من ذلك وغيره إنشاء وإفناء وإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like a crop, worldly life first flourishes and increases, then declines into extinction; its toil and anxieties make it unworthy of pride and a reason to seek lasting bliss.
rows.anchor: تقبل أولا في غاية النضرة والبهجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children are the greatest worldly adornments, yet they decay quickly, require effort, and may bring good if used to please God or become harm and disappointment.
rows.anchor: وهما أجل ما في هذه الدار من متاعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enduring righteous deeds are good works done solely for God’s sake, which the author says he has urged earlier.
rows.anchor: وهي أعمال الخير المجردة التي يقصد بها وجه الله تعالى التي رغبنا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to warn those heedless of remembrance, whose eyes and ears fail to take in the warning, about the greatest losers.
rows.anchor: إخبارا عظيما أيها التاركون من لا خالق ولا رازق لهم سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds vary: some worship angels, stars, prophets, or idols, while others commit different forms of unbelief.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من يعبد الملائكة , ومنهم من يعبد النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their effort went astray because they turned from the only one who can benefit or harm them toward things that do neither.
rows.anchor: الإعراض عمن لا ينفعهم ولا يضرهم إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the obvious failure, they imagine their work is expertly done because their judgment is weak.
rows.anchor: أي فعلا هو في غاية الإحكام

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī transmits from Saʿd that the greatest losers are Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, while Christians denied Paradise has food or drink.
rows.anchor: وروى البخاري في التفسير عن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه أن الأخسرين اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that both groups deny bodily resurrection and restrict the afterlife to a spiritual one.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال اليهود لأن الفريقين أنكروا الحشر الجسماني وخصوه بالروحاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their efforts fail because they disbelieve in God’s signs and meeting Him, leaving nothing to restrain their desires.
rows.anchor: فصاروا لا يخافون فلا يردهم شيء عن أهوائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their good deeds are null because they lack faith as their foundation.
rows.anchor: أي سقطت وبطلت وفسدت بسبب جحدهم للدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assigns them no weight on Judgment Day: no one can object to His majesty or intercede without His leave, and they ignored His signs and felt secure from His scheme.
rows.anchor: ما لنا من الكبرياء والعظمة المانعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is their recompense for disbelief and for mocking God’s signs and messengers; ridicule compounds their contempt beyond unbelief alone.
rows.anchor: فلم يكتفوا بالكفر الذي هو طعن في الإلهية حتى ضموا إليه الهزء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers with righteous deeds receive the gardens of al-Firdaws, the highest Paradise, as their welcome and lodging.
rows.anchor: أي أعلى الجنة , وأصله البستان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remain there and do not wish to leave; their pleasures have no limit, and long residence brings no boredom or desire for higher status.
rows.anchor: بل هم في غاية الرضى بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam’s purpose is to show God’s encompassing mercy through blessings on all creation, implying His perfections, power to create wonders, resurrection, and transcendence beyond having a child or peer.
rows.anchor: بيان اتصافه سبحانه بشمول الرحمة بإفاضة النعم علىجميع خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is named for Mary because her story most clearly demonstrates perfect power and knowledge, especially the extraordinary birth and Jesus’s speech, knowledge, and scripture in infancy.
rows.anchor: لأن قصتها أدل ما فيها على تمام القدرة وشمول العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s conception of a son without a man is the most extraordinary of the four human modes of generation, since the weaker sex bears the stronger.
rows.anchor: أن يتولد منها على ضعفها أقوى النوع وهو الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unusual dates from dry palm wood and water appearing in an unexpected place also illustrate divine power.
rows.anchor: في غير حينه من يابس الحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening letters’ articulation and qualities are read as signs; the author begins linking them to the initially weak position of God’s people before opponents.
rows.anchor: فالافتتاح بهذه الأحرف هنا إشارة - والله أعلم - إلى أن أهل الله عامة

rows.anchor: أن يتولد منها على ضعفها أقوى النوع وهو الذكر

rows.claim: The opening letters’ articulation and qualities are read as signs; the author begins linking them to the initially weak position of God’s people before opponents.
rows.anchor: فالافتتاح بهذه الأحرف هنا إشارة - والله أعلم - إلى أن أهل الله عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening letters symbolize stages in the Prophet’s mission: initially his message was known but met with limited opposition, then collective hostility made his position weak and obscure; the readings of hāʾ reflect concealment and some visibility.
rows.anchor: فإنه اشتهر أمره ولكنه كان ضعيفا بإنكار قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As opposition intensified, most Companions migrated to Abyssinia; Abū Ṭālib feared the Arab masses and composed his famous lāmiyya, and Quraysh later confined them in the defile.
rows.anchor: فهاجر أكثر الصحابة رضي الله عنهم إلى الحبشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The middle phase is linked to the effort by Quraysh to revoke the oppressive boycott and free the Muslims from the defile.
rows.anchor: هذا كما كان عند قيام من قام من قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Khadīja and Abū Ṭālib died, the Prophet was rejected at Ṭāʾif and needed a protector to return to Mecca; al-Muṭʿim b. ʿAdī granted protection and escorted him armed.
rows.anchor: ثم عند موت خديجة رضي الله عنها وأبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God caused al-Muṭʿim to die an unbeliever at Badr despite the Prophet’s efforts to protect him, showing that God chooses whom His general and special mercy reaches so sinners do not despair and the obedient do not presume safety.
rows.anchor: ثم قضى سبحانه أن قتل المطعم في بدر كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later phases combine hardship with powerful victory: the pledge of the Anṣār begins an ascent, and setbacks at Ḥunayn and Ṭāʾif are followed by fame and triumph.
rows.anchor: فإنه تعقبه قوة عظيمة بالإطباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter symbolism concerns God’s people generally, but Jesus is the surah’s central figure and the special referent of its signs.
rows.anchor: وأما ما يخص عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام الذي هو صورة سورتها ومطمح إشارتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is associated with qāf, whose articulation and qualities fit his life: Pharaoh killed Israelite boys in his birth year, and Moses’s killing of the Egyptian led to his flight and journey to God.
rows.anchor: فموسى عليه السلام أو أصحاب شرائعهم بمنزلة القاف التي هي من أقصى اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David is associated with hamza as the second scriptural figure among the Israelites; the author begins relating David to its articulation.
rows.anchor: وداود عليه السلام ثاني ذوي كتبهم بمنزلة الهمزة التي هي أبعد من مخرج الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David is associated with hamza as the second scriptural figure among the Israelites; the author begins relating David to its articulation.
rows.anchor: وداود عليه السلام ثاني ذوي كتبهم بمنزلة الهمزة التي هي أبعد من مخرج الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David’s letter traits reflect his kingship, victories, and public prominence, as well as the humility and repentance shown by his weeping and devotion.
rows.anchor: بما كان فيه من الملك والظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāf points to Jesus as a second lawgiver in the world, while hāʾ signals his descent from David; each shares qualities of the letter associated with him.
rows.anchor: فالكاف هنا إشارة إلى أن عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣād’s articulation and qualities symbolize the universal reach, exaltation, and dissemination of Jesus’s message, whose first stage combines strength with weakness.
rows.anchor: والصاد التي هي من طرف اللسان وهي خاتمة هذه الحروف إشارة مما فيها من الإطباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāʾ points to Jesus’s later concealment through ascent to heaven; its lowered articulation also indicates his place in the second heaven.
rows.anchor: إلى أن أمره يبطن بعد ذلك الظهور ويخفى بارتفاعه إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The voiced yāʾ signals Jesus’s descent and effective authority, while its qualities also indicate the limited number of followers at that time.
rows.anchor: وتدل بكونها من وسط اللسان على تمكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open, soft yāʾ points to Jesus’s victory over the Dajjāl among people afflicted by hardship before his descent.
rows.anchor: وتدل بانفتاحها ورخاوتها على ظهوره على الدجال في أولئك القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predominance of lowered articulation points to the episode of Gog and Magog, when God tells Jesus to lead His servants to Mount Ṭūr.
rows.anchor: عبادا لي لا يدان لأحد بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAyn’s middle articulation signals the people’s confinement, its voicing means enemies cannot reach them, and its other qualities indicate hardship ending well and victory.
rows.anchor: لا سبيل للعدو عليهم ولا وصول بوجه إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣād signifies greater strength without violence, applying to all people; its sibilance points to the trumpet, universal death, opened graves, and disclosure of hearts.
rows.anchor: وبالصفير على أنه ليس وراء ذلك إلا النفخ في الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letters’ order reflects God’s enduring pattern among the chosen and His complete power, knowledge, and wisdom; He saves them from arrogant hardness and humiliation.
rows.anchor: وترتيب هذه الحروف على هذا النظم الدال عليه دائر على القدرة التامة والعلم الشامل والحكمة الباهرة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī explains the opening letters as praise by which God praises Himself.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى ما قال الكلبي : هو ثناء أثنى الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as free of deficiency and able to do all He wills, al-Raḥmān as generous to all creatures, and al-Raḥīm as granting the righteous their desired happiness.
rows.anchor: الذي عم نواله سائر مخلوقاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David’s letter traits reflect his kingship, victories, and public prominence, as well as the humility and repentance shown by his weeping and devotion.
rows.anchor: بما كان فيه من الملك والظهور

rows.claim: Ṣād’s articulation and qualities symbolize the universal reach, exaltation, and dissemination of Jesus’s message, whose first stage combines strength with weakness.
rows.anchor: والصاد التي هي من طرف اللسان وهي خاتمة هذه الحروف إشارة مما فيها من الإطباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāʾ points to Jesus’s later concealment through ascent to heaven; its lowered articulation also indicates his place in the second heaven.
rows.anchor: إلى أن أمره يبطن بعد ذلك الظهور ويخفى بارتفاعه إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The voiced yāʾ signals Jesus’s descent and effective authority, while its qualities also indicate the limited number of followers at that time.
rows.anchor: وتدل بكونها من وسط اللسان على تمكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open, soft yāʾ points to Jesus’s victory over the Dajjāl among people afflicted by hardship before his descent.
rows.anchor: وتدل بانفتاحها ورخاوتها على ظهوره على الدجال في أولئك القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predominance of lowered articulation points to the episode of Gog and Magog, when God tells Jesus to lead His servants to Mount Ṭūr.
rows.anchor: عبادا لي لا يدان لأحد بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAyn’s middle articulation signals the people’s confinement, its voicing means enemies cannot reach them, and its other qualities indicate hardship ending well and victory.
rows.anchor: لا سبيل للعدو عليهم ولا وصول بوجه إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣād signifies greater strength without violence, applying to all people; its sibilance points to the trumpet, universal death, opened graves, and disclosure of hearts.
rows.anchor: وبالصفير على أنه ليس وراء ذلك إلا النفخ في الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letters’ order reflects God’s enduring pattern among the chosen and His complete power, knowledge, and wisdom; He saves them from arrogant hardness and humiliation.
rows.anchor: وترتيب هذه الحروف على هذا النظم الدال عليه دائر على القدرة التامة والعلم الشامل والحكمة الباهرة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī explains the opening letters as praise by which God praises Himself.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى ما قال الكلبي : هو ثناء أثنى الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as free of deficiency and able to do all He wills, al-Raḥmān as generous to all creatures, and al-Raḥīm as granting the righteous their desired happiness.
rows.anchor: الذي عم نواله سائر مخلوقاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding surah showed the Qur’an to be upright and without deviation, through well-told stories, wisdom, and meanings refuting claims that God has a child, and it closed with scripture, monotheism, and righteous action.
rows.anchor: مقصود التي قبلها الدلالة على أنم القرآن قيم لا عوج فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam opens with stories still more astonishing than those of the Cave, told with new details that do not contradict earlier accounts and demonstrate the inexhaustible wonders of revelation.
rows.anchor: بسياق غير ما تقدم فيما مضى عن السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s figures are monotheist leaders and reformers who practiced righteousness and rejected shirk; Jews prompted Quraysh to ask about the Cave and Dhū al-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: سادة الموحدين ، وقادة المصلحين المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Jews expect Jesus to come in the future, when people will follow one religion, and reads this as evidence of God’s transcendence beyond offspring and His power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: ويكون الناس في أيامه على دين واحد تصديقا لوعد التوارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah begins with Zechariah and John because the miraculous child most forcefully rebukes the Jews, who killed both father and son; righteous monotheism also secures answered prayer despite extraordinary circumstances.
rows.anchor: وكان تقديم قصته أولى لأن التبكيت به أعظم لمباشرتهم لقتله وقتل ابنه يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next story concerns Jesus, whom the Jews falsely claimed as God’s son and sought to kill; it rebukes them over Zechariah and John, their claim of crucifixion, and their slander of Mary, while proving resurrection.
rows.anchor: وثنى بأمر من نسبوء إليه وافتروه عليه وقصدوا قتله على وجه معرب عن شأنه

rows.anchor: وثنى بأمر من نسبوء إليه وافتروه عليه وقصدوا قتله على وجه معرب عن شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quotes Jacob’s Torah prophecy that Judah’s scepter and rule will remain until the one to whom kingship belongs arrives, whom the nations await.
rows.anchor: لا يعدم سبط يهوذا ملكا مسلطا وأفخاده نبيا مرسلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews identify the awaited figure as the Messiah and Mahdi, expecting him to rescue them from humiliation.
rows.anchor: يسمونه مع ذلك المنتظر والمهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a dialogue, a Jew objected that Jesus had not possessed universal rule; the author answered that Jesus will return following Islam, all the earth will follow him, and the prophecy does not limit his rule to his first coming.
rows.anchor: حين ينزل تابعا لديننا من حيث إنه لا يقبل إلا الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jew later showed the author a commentary saying the Messiah may appear to Israel, disappear, then reappear and have universal authority; the author saw this as confirmation, but the Jew deferred belief to God’s will.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يبدو لإسرائيل ثم يختقي ثم يظهر فيكون له الكل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Maryam follows the Cave’s stories with marvels even more astonishing and obscure in cause, beginning with John’s birth to elderly Zechariah and his barren wife.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير في برهانه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr compares Jesus’s conception without a father with the earlier marvels and says God alone acts: causes produce effects only according to His custom, not by necessity.
rows.anchor: ليعلم أن الأسباب في الحقيقة لا يتوقف عليها شيء من مسبباتها إلا بحسب سنة الله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He links the answer that John’s birth is easy for God to the reminder that Zechariah was created before he existed, then notes John received wisdom as a child and Mary and Jesus follow.
rows.anchor: ثم أتبع سبحانه بشارة زكريا بيحيى بإتيانه الحكم صبيا
